# #1697: Patch: the AI's own games can carry dealt decks, last boards and Glitch boards, so the cards that read them can be measured
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The AI's self-play games — the ones its quality gates, sweeps and card-health reports run — always start from a plain deal. But some cards only work with setup a real match carries: Portal to the Past needs your previous game's board, a Glitch reads the Glitch boards, dealt-deck cards need dealt seats. In the AI's own games those cards literally cannot act, so every 'never played' and win-rate measurement of them measures an empty start, not the card — Portal to the Past is already flagged at-risk as 'never played' although it was affordable on 20 turns across the measured games. After this, a self-play game can be configured with the same setup inputs the server gives real matches.

## Why

- `MatchConfig` (`crates/ai/src/match_.rs`) is `{seed, decks, handicaps, controllers, max_actions}` and `play_match` builds `CreateGameOptions` with `..default()` — there is no way to pass `dealt`, `last_boards`, `glitch_boards` or `custom`, though `create_game` accepts all of them (`crates/engine/src/state.rs`).
- Concrete consequence: `classicplus-029` is recorded 'at risk … affordable on 20 turns over 8 games, never played' (`crates/ai/src/shadow_ban.rs`) in games where the card can do nothing — an empty last board gives nothing (R129). The fuzz already draws these inputs; the AI runner can't.

## Proposal

Add optional `dealt`/`last_boards`/`glitch_boards` fields to `MatchConfig` (serde defaults; unset means today's behavior, so every seeded game and fold is unchanged), plumb them through `create_game` in `play_match`, and expose them on the dev-run/sweep configuration so a measurement can opt in — for example carrying the previous game's last board into the next, as the server does. `custom` needs the Luau host and stays out of scope.

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/{match_.rs,dev_run.rs,sweep.rs,gate.rs,config.rs}`. Spec R417, R433, R564, R678, §9.9.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `MatchConfig` with `last_boards` lets Portal to the Past resolve in a seeded test.
- [ ] With the fields unset, existing seeded matches replay identically (byte-for-byte compatible).
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` green; the `gate` smoke is unaffected.

## Size and risks

Small-medium — plumbing only, no policy or ban change. Deliberately scoped: it makes the setup-input cards measurable; what the sweeps do with the new measurements is the existing lane's work. Dealt seats must respect the same deck-legality rules the fuzz and server apply.

## Risks

- **Determinism and replay.** Unset inputs must give exactly today's `CreateGameOptions` and `FoldArgs`. Every literal gets `MatchSetup::default()`, never a filled value. The unset test and the ai_slow gate smokes hold this.
- **Serde.** `#[serde(flatten)]` takes no other attribute on the field. The inner fields carry `default` and `skip_serializing_if`, so the JSON with nothing set is unchanged; the JSON tests hold this. No caller deserialises `MatchConfig` today.
- **Dev-run purity.** `stats` plays games in parallel chunks, so a setup must be the same for every game. Carrying game n−1's board into game n would break chunking (rejected).
- **Hidden information.** Nothing changes: the engine freezes the boards, and `redact` keeps only the AI's own last board (R185).
- **Deck legality.** `create_game` validates every deck whatever `dealt` says, so dealt seats meet the same rules as the fuzz and the server.
- **Unused imports.** Once `FoldArgs` leaves `gate.rs` and `dev_run.rs`, clippy fails until the import goes.

## Open questions

These were decided here, and a person may overrule them:
1. **One grouped field, not three.** The three inputs are one `MatchSetup`, flattened, rather than three fields. The JSON is the same, and each literal site takes one line instead of three.
2. **No carry mode.** There is no "carry the previous game's last board" mode, because it breaks the dev run's per-game purity. A caller sets static inputs.
3. **No CLI flags.** There are no `cargo jackioh stats/sweep` flags, since the issue keeps the work in `crates/ai` and leaves what the sweeps measure to their own lane.
4. **Sweep boards in seat order.** The sweep's inputs are in seat order, not by role (AI or greedy).
5. **`config.rs` unchanged.** No new number is needed.

## Risks

- **Determinism and replay.** Unset inputs must give exactly today's `CreateGameOptions` and `FoldArgs`. Every literal gets `MatchSetup::default()`, never a filled value. The unset test and the ai_slow gate smokes hold this.
- **Serde.** `#[serde(flatten)]` takes no other attribute on the field. The inner fields carry `default` and `skip_serializing_if`, so the JSON with nothing set is unchanged; the JSON tests hold this. No caller deserialises `MatchConfig` today.
- **Dev-run purity.** `stats` plays games in parallel chunks, so a setup must be the same for every game. Carrying game n−1's board into game n would break chunking (rejected).
- **Hidden information.** Nothing changes: the engine freezes the boards, and `redact` keeps only the AI's own last board (R185).
- **Deck legality.** `create_game` validates every deck whatever `dealt` says, so dealt seats meet the same rules as the fuzz and the server.
- **Unused imports.** Once `FoldArgs` leaves `gate.rs` and `dev_run.rs`, clippy fails until the import goes.

## Open questions

These were decided here, and a person may overrule them:
1. **One grouped field, not three.** The three inputs are one `MatchSetup`, flattened, rather than three fields. The JSON is the same, and each literal site takes one line instead of three.
2. **No carry mode.** There is no "carry the previous game's last board" mode, because it breaks the dev run's per-game purity. A caller sets static inputs.
3. **No CLI flags.** There are no `cargo jackioh stats/sweep` flags, since the issue keeps the work in `crates/ai` and leaves what the sweeps measure to their own lane.
4. **Sweep boards in seat order.** The sweep's inputs are in seat order, not by role (AI or greedy).
5. **`config.rs` unchanged.** No new number is needed.

- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` is green; `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke) passes as on main (acceptance 3).
- [ ] The tools and server tests compile and pass.
- [ ] rustfmt, clippy (workspace, `-D warnings`), the catalog, patches and rulings checks and the workspace cargo tests are green; `apps/web/src/wire` is unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` reports no problem (expected kind Internal or AI, no card).
- [ ] The README is updated.

## Risks

- **Determinism and replay.** Unset inputs must give exactly today's `CreateGameOptions` and `FoldArgs`. Every literal gets `MatchSetup::default()`, never a filled value. The unset test and the ai_slow gate smokes hold this.
- **Serde.** `#[serde(flatten)]` takes no other attribute on the field. The inner fields carry `default` and `skip_serializing_if`, so the JSON with nothing set is unchanged; the JSON tests hold this. No caller deserialises `MatchConfig` today.
- **Dev-run purity.** `stats` plays games in parallel chunks, so a setup must be the same for every game. Carrying game n−1's board into game n would break chunking (rejected).
- **Hidden information.** Nothing changes: the engine freezes the boards, and `redact` keeps only the AI's own last board (R185).
- **Deck legality.** `create_game` validates every deck whatever `dealt` says, so dealt seats meet the same rules as the fuzz and the server.
- **Unused imports.** Once `FoldArgs` leaves `gate.rs` and `dev_run.rs`, clippy fails until the import goes.

## Open questions

These were decided here, and a person may overrule them:
1. **One grouped field, not three.** The three inputs are one `MatchSetup`, flattened, rather than three fields. The JSON is the same, and each literal site takes one line instead of three.
2. **No carry mode.** There is no "carry the previous game's last board" mode, because it breaks the dev run's per-game purity. A caller sets static inputs.
3. **No CLI flags.** There are no `cargo jackioh stats/sweep` flags, since the issue keeps the work in `crates/ai` and leaves what the sweeps measure to their own lane.
4. **Sweep boards in seat order.** The sweep's inputs are in seat order, not by role (AI or greedy).
5. **`config.rs` unchanged.** No new number is needed.
